item.title: Dual-functional-unit modulation enables superior energy storage in high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics
item.description:
این مقاله با مدولاسیون واحدهای دوگانه عملکردی، ذخیره‌سازی انرژی را در فروالکتریک‌های ریلکسور با آنتروپی بالا بهبود می‌دهد.
Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in dual-functional-unit modulation via configurational-entropy engineering, simultaneously tailoring local polarization configurations and oxygen octahedral tilt in Bi0.47Na0.47Ba0.06TiO3 ceramics. Combined with grain refinement, this overcomes the polarization–breakdown trade-off, achieving 16.19 J cm−3 recoverable energy density and 91.3% efficiency, establishing a general design principle for high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics in dielectric energy storage.

item.description:

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in discovering temperature-dependent Li-Ag alloying kinetics as the failure mechanism in anodeless all-solid-state pouch cells at low temperatures, and in proposing a brief 45 °C formation charge that permanently activates the Ag-C interlayer. This scalable, material-agnostic protocol enables efficient Li transport at 5 °C, retaining 87% capacity after 250 cycles—tripling output versus fixed-temperature cycling—extending sub-ambient operation without redesign.

Nature Communications | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 The novelty lies in using interpretable machine learning plus DFT to screen thousands of active sites, identifying Ni-Co dual-atom catalysts that shift oxygen redox from the two-electron to a four-electron LiOH pathway. Significance: ~60,000 mAh g⁻¹ capacity, 2075 stable cycles with reduced voltage decay, and dual function as a multifunctional protective layer suppressing lithium dendrites—enabling high-energy lithium–oxygen batteries.

ACS Nano | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in revealing nonmonotonic Zn(TFA)2 dissolution governed by a concentration-dependent hydrolysis-coordination balance, and using acetonitrile to widen the clear-solution window. This enables anion-derived interphases suppressing water reactions, yielding ultralong Zn//Zn cycling (8200 h at −25 °C) and high-retention Zn//PANI and Zn//I2 cells. It reframes electrolyte design around speciation and accessible solvation states rather than reported solubility.

💡 The novelty lies in revealing that fluorinated ether solvents, considered non-solvating diluents, selectively solvate high-electron-donating anions via cation-solvent-anion ternary interactions. This revises conventional solvation views and offers a molecular framework for electrolyte design. Its significance is suppressing polysulfide shuttling, improving Li°||S cycling stability, and guiding solvent design for high-energy monovalent cation batteries.

item.title: Electric‐Field Responsive Molecular Switch Unlocks Stable 4.5 V‐Class Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
item.description:

Angewandte Chemie International Edition | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in defining an electric field coupling agent that acts as a threshold-gated molecular switch, activated only above a critical interfacial field. This enables a self-limiting, gradient boron-rich interphase, achieving field-enhanced stability. Significance: it delivers stable 4.5 V sodium layered oxide cathodes (87.9% retention over 1000 cycles, 1 Ah pouch cells), offering a generalizable paradigm for on-demand high-voltage battery protection.

National Science Review | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in revealing that M–N4 single-atom catalysts, while lowering charge overpotential, also increase Li2O2 reactivity toward ether electrolytes, causing carboxylate accumulation and cathode passivation—an overlooked activity–stability trade-off. Significance: this mechanistic insight enables a localized high-concentration electrolyte that suppresses side reactions and extends cycling from 42 to 398 cycles, guiding stable catalyst/electrolyte interface design for high-energy Li–O2 batteries.
🏷 Li-O2 battery · single-atom catalyst · Li2O2 interface · electrolyte design · cycling stability
